linhas.en:
That which symbolizes Gilgamesh's youth.
It represents his quest for immortality and why.

             ◆

And so, that childhood of his came to an end.
The tyrant that shed neither blood nor tears.
The hero who enjoyed himself, indulging in every treasure,
every pleasure.

A king with the conviction to commit good and evil alike.
Since the absolute standard is "himself,"
he has no need for other ideologies or ways of life.
His conceit is equal to the Macedonian King of Conquerors,
but the main difference between the King of Heroes and
the King of Conquerors is that he "does not need vassals."

This hero, from beginning to end, ruled only "himself."
What he loved were simply treasures, tools;
people were only things fated to disappear.

……even if he recognized
how much they deserved to be loved.

             ◆

The themes in "CCC" make talking about women unavoidable.
This is a tangent, but Gilgamesh's preferred type is
"a noble #RUBS  maiden#RUBEvirgin#REND."
(As a child, his type was "a flower blooming in the wild.")
It seems he hates women who, while reliant on men,
are using them on the inside.
